name: Hydrogen Ground State
description: A single hydrogen atom: 1 proton and 1 electron in the 1s orbital

layman.title: The Simplest Atom
layman.summary: Meet hydrogen — the most basic building block of the universe

sections.whatsHappening: You're looking at a single hydrogen atom — the simplest atom that exists. At the center is a proton (red), a positively charged particle. Surrounding it is a cloud of probability (blue) showing where the electron is likely to be found. The electron isn't orbiting like a planet — it exists as a fuzzy cloud of possibility.
sections.whyItMatters: Hydrogen makes up about three quarters of the ordinary matter in the universe, by mass. Every star, including our Sun, is mostly hydrogen. Understanding this one atom is the foundation for understanding all of chemistry and most of physics.
sections.whatToWatch: Notice the blue cloud around the proton. This is the electron's '1s orbital'. It is round, which means the electron is equally likely to be found in any direction from the proton. The outer surface marks where the electron is found 90% of the time (141 pm from the proton); the brighter inner shell marks its single most likely distance (52.9 pm, the Bohr radius).
sections.funFact: If the electron cloud were a stadium 200 m across, the proton at its center would be about 1.2 mm across: a coarse grain of sand. Atoms are almost entirely empty space!

scientific.narrative: The hydrogen atom is shown in its ground state with principal quantum number n=1, angular momentum quantum number l=0, and magnetic quantum number m=0. The electron probability density is given by the square of the 1s wavefunction, which is spherically symmetric. The radial probability peaks at the Bohr radius (52.9 pm from the nucleus). The cloud's outer surface is drawn at r = 2.66 a₀ (141 pm), which encloses 90% of the probability; the inner shell is drawn at the most likely distance, r = a₀.
